observations:
Torah #203 has zero bechina edges in torahData.js. The source text contains exactly one bechina declaration: 'וְאֶסְתֵּר הִיא הַשְּׁכִינָה' (Esther IS the Shechina). This yields a single 2-node component (אסתר ↔ שכינה), which is captured as Package 1 in torah_203_packages.json.

The question for this file is: does Torah #203 contain any independent conceptual domain that cannot be accommodated within that one package, and that has enough concepts (3+) to constitute a new package? The answer is no.

All other concepts in the source text are either:
(a) Eitza-related: 'סִפּוּרֵי דִּבְרֵי הַנָּשִׁים' (women's stories), 'חֲצַר בֵּית הַנָּשִׁים' (the women's courtyard), and 'מַעֲמַד הַשְּׁכִינָה' (the state of the Shechina) are all components of the eitza structure — they describe the mechanism (stories) and the result (knowledge of the Shechina's state). They are not bechina-equivalent concepts; they are cause-and-effect links.
(b) Narrative/biographical: Mordechai functions as the proof-verse figure who demonstrated the practice. The text does not declare him a bechina of any abstract concept within this Torah.

The Torah's argument follows a single-step structure:
  [Pkg 1: Esther = Shechina] → (proof-verse + eitza) → knowledge of the Shechina's state through women's stories.

There is no secondary domain, no evil mirror cluster, no letter-symbolism package, and no independent thematic family with 3 or more bechina-connected nodes. The teaching is structurally minimal: one bechina pair at the foundation, and one eitza flowing from it.

Conclusion: Package 1 (אֶסְתֵּר וְהַשְּׁכִינָה) is the complete and sole package for Torah #203. No new packages are needed beyond what is documented in torah_203_packages.json.
